history.name: Wiring into a coding agent
history.description: Setup appends a short stanza to whichever agent instruction files the repo already has — CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .cursor/rules, .github/copilot-instructions.md or .windsurfrules — and creates AGENTS.md when there are none. The stanza is a pointer rather than a copy: it names six commands, the tone the project writes in, the line between recording a change and rewording an entry, and the rule that a feature change is not finished until the ledger records it. The --agents flag chooses the files, and changing the tone rewrites the stanza in every one of them.

Setup appends a short stanza to whichever agent instruction files the repo already has, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .cursor/rules, .github/copilot-instructions.md or .windsurfrules, and creates AGENTS.md when there are none. The stanza is a pointer rather than a copy: the commands, the tone, how to record what moved and why, the line between recording a change and rewording an entry, and the rule that the agent never commits.

events.what: The stanza tells an agent to record a change as what and why, to name the code a new feature lives in, and to leave a reason it doesn't know as a question.
events.why: That is how a change is recorded now, and the stanza is often all an agent reads before it records one.

events.what: The stanza tells an agent to record what moved in a sentence a client could read, to say how to see it when it knows, and not to commit, prepare or cut unless asked.
events.why: Coding agents never commit for the developer, and the free preview reads well only if the recorded facts do.
